summary: RE-TEST of Howard's walk fixes on EST-886440 (image-scan blueprint). All 8 required flows verified end-to-end in real browser against the public URL. Results: login OK, modal opens; page 1 'FRONT & REAR ELEVATIONS' is correctly AMBIGUOUS — no face preselected and picker shows 'PAGE DIDN'T IDENTIFY ONE — PICK IT'; drawing a polygon with NO face raises the exact refusal toast "Pick a face for this view first — the page didn't identify one, so it won't be guessed" and no zone is created; Read (AI) refuses on this scan with toast 'This page has no recorded render DPI (a scan) — trace the scale by hand instead' and scale-missing stays visible; Trace scale (24 ft) confirms and the scale-ok label reads exactly '✓ TRACE · you calibrated 24 ft' (no 'read from sheet' text); Draw+Convert produces zone 'siding · back · 60.42 ft²' and impact row 'Vinyl Siding · 1 ZONE · app 44 → you 0.6 SQ (60.42 ft²)'; per-wall panel visible listing FRONT 920 / BACK 1160 / LEFT 1091 (wall 780 · gable 311) / RIGHT 1091 (wall 780 · gable 311); delete removes the zone with toast "Zone deleted — the app's own number is back". Estimate left clean. Backend not tested per request. All four fixed behaviors (a-d) are working correctly.

ui_bugs.issue: When a polygon draw is refused because no face is picked, the draft points are NOT cleared. If the user then picks a face and clicks 4 new corners, those points are APPENDED to the stale draft (now 8 vertices) and the 'click near first vertex' close no longer works because the first vertex is the stale one from the refused attempt. Reproduced deterministically in the first automated run — required an Escape key press between attempts to get a clean draw. Human-facing effect: after seeing the 'pick a face' toast, the user's next polygon silently fails to close.

action_items: In PdfOverlayEditor.jsx finalizeDraft: also call setDraft(null) on the refusal branch (missing faceId), so a subsequent draw starts with an empty draft after the user picks a face. Same for the pageScale-missing warning path (currently only shows a warning toast but still saves — that's fine). Two-line fix: add `setDraft(null);` before the `return` inside `if (!faceId)`.
critical_code_review_comments: finalizeDraft refusal path leaks state — the returned-early branch keeps the previous points in `draft`, coupling the refusal UX to a keyboard shortcut (Escape) that isn't advertised.
faceFromTitle correctly returns '' on 0 or >1 hits (verified live on page 1 'FRONT & REAR ELEVATIONS' and page 2 'LEFT & RIGHT ELEVATIONS') — good.
readPrintedScale guards on `!renderDpi` and shows the correct scan-instead-trace toast — good.
confirmScale sets `source: 'TRACE · you calibrated N ft'` and scale-ok reads exactly that — matches spec 'label contains TRACE (NOT read from sheet)'.
per-wall panel is rendered read-only from `perWall` prop with a clear 'not bound' note — good.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 8 required flows pass; 1 medium bug found (stale draft after face-refusal) that does NOT block any of the required assertions.

seed_data_creation: None persisted. The single zone drawn (siding/back on page 1) was deleted; delete toast confirmed the app's number is back. Estimate 1f8b8b60-4b19-48eb-b1b5-0371276c8645 is clean.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All four Howard-walk fixes verified on EST-886440: (1) face is NOT auto-defaulted on the two-face 'FRONT & REAR ELEVATIONS' page and drawing is refused with a clear toast; (2) READ(AI) refuses on this scan (no render_dpi) telling the user to trace; (3) after tracing 24 ft the scale label reads '✓ TRACE · you calibrated 24 ft' — the word 'TRACE' appears and 'read from sheet' does not; (4) per-wall panel is visible with front/back/left/right areas (BACK=1160 ft² matches the 1,160 ft² rear-wall pin from the pytest suite). One MEDIUM bug worth fixing next iteration: refused draws leave stale points in the draft, so subsequent draws after picking a face won't close via 'click near first' unless Escape is pressed first.
rca of the issue: finalizeDraft returns early on `!faceId` without clearing `draft.points`. Next mouseDown events append to the stale array; the polygon's 'close by proximity to points[0]' compares new clicks against the OLD first vertex (from the refused attempt) which is far from the new draw region. Mitigation: `setDraft(null)` inside the refusal branch.
